standard_prerequisites.name: The notions of a finite partition of a topological space and of a finite stratification (a finite partition into locally closed pieces), and the fact that the closure of a piece is closed
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on partitions and stratifications, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the object to be constructed and the pieces from which it is built.

core_obligations: The closure and boundary of a piece: for each member of the partition the proof forms its closure and the difference between that closure and the piece itself (proof lines 5814).
The family of intersections: it then considers the finite family of all intersections of the closures and of those differences, one choice per index (proof lines 5815-5816).

Local closedness: the author notes that the members of this finite family are closed subsets whose differences, restricted to the right piece, are locally closed, which is what makes the family a stratification (proof lines 5817-5819).
Conclusion: taking the non-empty members among these intersections gives a finite stratification refining the given partition (proof lines 5819-5820).
proof_roadmap: 对划分的每一块取闭包 T_i 与其差 Δ_i = T_i \ X_i。
考虑所有「每个下标取 T_i 或 Δ_i」的有限交之族 S；其元素是闭集，且在每个 X_i 上恰给出局部闭的分解，去掉空集后即为细化原划分的有限分层。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement says that every finite partition of a topological space is refined by a finite stratification (author lemma at source lines 5807-5811, label lemma-partition-refined-by-stratification). The proof (source lines 5813-5821) constructs the refinement explicitly: from each piece it forms the closure and the difference between the closure and the piece, and then takes the finite family of all intersections choosing one of the two for each index; the resulting non-empty members form a finite stratification refining the partition (proof lines 5814-5819). The lemma is the technical device by which the chapter passes from partitions to stratifications. H2.
